description:
Pulsar Code is a team of four from India, bringing together data analysis, web development, design, and all-round support to build a solution for the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge. We’re focused on making NISAR’s synthetic aperture radar data easier to understand and act on.

Team lineup

• Kairav Singh — Data Collection & Analyst (India)

Gathers and processes the mission’s raw SAR data, turning scattered radar outputs into clean, structured datasets. Runs the analysis that forms the backbone of the project’s insights.

• Akashdeep Singh — Web Developer (India)

Builds and maintains the project’s website, bringing the team’s data and findings to life as a functional, accessible platform.

• Prabhpreet Singh — Designer (India)

Shapes the visual identity of the project — UI, branding, and overall look — making the SAR data as easy to read as it is to see.

• Satgur Singh — Support & Operations (India)

Pitches in across every workstream, from research to testing to coordination, keeping the team moving and filling gaps wherever they appear.
summary:
SARS WATCH is an interactive satellite-based flood monitoring and historical analysis platform designed to help users identify, visualize, and understand flood events using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery.

The platform integrates satellite data, including NISAR and Sentinel-1, to support the detection and analysis of flood-affected regions across different time periods. Unlike conventional optical satellite imagery, SAR technology can capture useful surface information even under cloudy conditions and at night.

Users can explore historical flood events, visualize satellite observations, compare affected areas, and understand how flood patterns change over time through an interactive web interface.

The project combines Python-based development, satellite data processing, geospatial visualization, and web technologies to make complex Earth observation data more accessible and understandable.

Our goal is to support disaster awareness, historical flood assessment, and more informed decision-making by transforming satellite observations into meaningful visual insights.
